newsitem.title: USA: Aspen Bancshares details deal with Zions.
newsitem.headline: Aspen Bancshares details deal with Zions.

text.p: Aspen Bancshares Inc Friday detailed pricing alternatives in its merger agreement with Zions Bancorporation
It said it took the step in response to the 45 percent rise in Zion's stock price since November 19 and numerous inquiries about the pricing provisions of the definitive agreement.
The companies announced on November 20 a definitive merger deal in which Aspen would be acquired in exchange for common shares of Zions.
Aspen, with assets of about $450 million, is the largest banking company headquartered in western Colorado.
Zions, based in Salt Lake City, has assets of about $6.5 billion and operates in Utah, Arizona and Nevada.

Aspen said that the purchase price for the deal is the sum of $73 million, Aspen's undistributed net income (or loss) from July 1, 1996 through the last day of the calendar month preceding the closing date, the daily average income (or loss) from this period multiplied by the number of days in the month up to the closing date, and contributions to capital from the exercise of Aspen stock options after June 30, 1996.
Aspen said its undistributed net income from July 1, 1996, through January 31 was about $1.55 million, an amount it said would likely change by the deal's closing date.
Transaction costs, currently estimated at $1.5 million, will be deducted from the purchase price, it said.

The total number of shares of Zions paid to Aspen shareholders will be determined by dividing the purchase price by the average closing price of Zions' stock, or, if such price is less than $83 or more than $93 per share, a "collar" arrangement will apply.
Several alternatives are available to determine the collar.
